sections.content: You know *es importante que* + subjunctive from A2 Unit 27. Here you use it with more evaluative expressions: *es fundamental que*, *es necesario que* and *es conveniente que*. They take the present subjunctive when they evaluate or require an action, and the subject of the second clause can be different.

items.spanish: Es importante que escuchemos opiniones diferentes antes de decidir.
items.english: It is important that we listen to different opinions before deciding.

items.spanish: Es fundamental que la discusión sea respetuosa.
items.english: It is fundamental that the discussion be respectful.

items.spanish: Es necesario que consideremos la evidencia disponible.
items.english: It is necessary that we consider the available evidence.

items.spanish: Es conveniente que la propuesta tenga objetivos claros.
items.english: It is advisable that the proposal have clear objectives.

sections.content: Remember: after *es necesario que* and similar expressions, the verb that follows is in the subjunctive: *Es necesario que lo revisemos.* not *Es necesario que lo revisamos.*
